To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alpha1-adrengeric stimulation induces hypertrophy in protein kinas C down-regulated cardiac myocytes.
phenylephrine induces hypertrophy in cultured neonatal cardiac myocytes even after PKC down-regulation.
PKC down-regulation does not inhibit phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy of cultured neonatal rat cardiac myocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein kinase C in the induction of cardiac hypertrophy by alpha 1-adrenergically mediated stimulation.
the effects of PKC on alpha1-adrengeric stimulation in the hypertrophy of cardiac myocytes.
the role of PKC in alpha1-adrengeric stimulation induced myocyte hypertrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alpha1-adrengeric stimulation induced hypertrophic response in cultured cardiac myocyte is not dependent upon PKC activation.
PKC activation plays a role in the hypertrophic response of cardiac myocytes to alpha1-adrenerigic stimulation but is not essential.
PKC is not essential for alpha1-adrenergy-induced hypertrophy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PKC down-regulation does not prevent alpha1-adrenergy induced hypertrophy, and the hypertrophic effect may be mediated by other signaling pathways such as tyrosine kinases.
alpha1-adrenergy stimulation may induce cardiac myocyte hypertrophic response by the activation of PKC independent pathway(s).
alpha1-adrenoceptors mediate the hypertrophic response of cardiac myocytes by a pathway independent of conventional PKC activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PKC is not essential for alpha1-adrengic receptor mediated hypertrophy.
PKC activation may be a secondary event in the hypertrophic signaling pathway induced by alpha1-adrenoceptor activation.
PKC activation may be necessary but not sufficient for the induction of myocyte hypertrophy.
